```{python}
import json
from pathlib import Path

import plotly.graph_objects as go
from IPython.display import Markdown

DATA = json.loads((Path.cwd() / "data" / "dashboard.json").read_text())

BAR = "#1f6feb"
MUTED = "#8b949e"


def bar(labels, values, title, xaxis):

    """
    Horizontal bar, highest at the top. Plotly draws category axes bottom-up, so
    the lists are reversed to put the leader where a reader looks first.
    """

    figure = go.Figure(
        go.Bar(x=values[::-1], y=labels[::-1], orientation="h", marker_color=BAR)
    )
    figure.update_layout(
        title=title,
        xaxis_title=xaxis,
        height=max(320, 26 * len(labels)),
        margin=dict(l=10, r=10, t=50, b=40),
        template="plotly_white",
    )
    return figure
```

```{python}
Markdown(f"""
Season **{DATA['season']}**, refreshed {DATA['generated_at']}.
Built from {DATA['totals']['matches']:,} matches and {DATA['totals']['goals']:,} goals
across {DATA['totals']['teams']} clubs and {DATA['totals']['players']:,} players.
""")
```

## This season

### Standings

Points follow the 3/1/0 rule, computed here rather than stored in the warehouse:
one match distributes points to two teams, so there is no single column to hold
them at the match grain.

```{python}
rows = DATA["standings"]

header = ["#", "Club", "P", "W pts", "GF", "GA", "GD"]
cells = [
    list(range(1, len(rows) + 1)),
    [r["team_name"] for r in rows],
    [r["played"] for r in rows],
    [r["points"] for r in rows],
    [r["goals_for"] for r in rows],
    [r["goals_against"] for r in rows],
    [f"{r['goal_difference']:+d}" for r in rows],
]

figure = go.Figure(
    go.Table(
        header=dict(values=header, fill_color="#f0f3f6", align="left"),
        cells=dict(values=cells, align="left", height=26),
        columnwidth=[0.5, 4, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1],
    )
)
figure.update_layout(height=max(320, 30 * len(rows) + 60), margin=dict(l=0, r=0, t=10, b=0))
figure
```

### Top scorers

Own goals are excluded: the source credits them to the player who scored into
his own net.

```{python}
rows = DATA["top_scorers_season"]
bar(
    [r["player_name"] for r in rows],
    [r["goals"] for r in rows],
    f"Top scorers, {DATA['season']}",
    "Goals",
)
```

## Since 2006

### Most wins

```{python}
rows = DATA["most_wins_all_time"]
bar(
    [r["team_name"] for r in rows],
    [r["wins"] for r in rows],
    "Most wins, all seasons",
    "Wins",
)
```

### Top scorers, all time

::: {.callout-warning}
## Read this chart with care

OpenLigaDB assigns more than one player id to the same person. Franck Ribery
appears under three, and they overlap inside a single season, so career totals
are split and this ranking understates several players. Resolving it means
entity matching, which is out of scope for this project. Current-season figures
are unaffected, because recent seasons use consistent ids.
:::

```{python}
rows = DATA["top_scorers_all_time"]
bar(
    [r["player_name"] for r in rows],
    [r["goals"] for r in rows],
    "Top scorers, all seasons",
    "Goals",
)
```

### Matches hosted by venue

```{python}
missing = DATA["matches_without_venue"]
total = DATA["totals"]["matches"]

Markdown(f"""
::: {{.callout-important}}
## Partial coverage

{missing:,} of {total:,} matches ({missing / total:.0%}) carry no usable venue in the
source, either a null reference or a blank stadium name, and are excluded below.
Older seasons are the worst affected, so read this as a recent-seasons ranking
rather than a complete history.
:::
""") if missing else Markdown("")
```

```{python}
rows = DATA["matches_by_venue"]
bar(
    [f"{r['location_stadium']} ({r['location_city']})" for r in rows],
    [r["matches"] for r in rows],
    "Matches hosted",
    "Matches",
)
```
